formulas.name: SPFM (Single-Point Fault Metric)

variables.meaning: sum of failure rates of all safety-related hardware elements

formulas.known_uncertainty: Exact clause number for the formula statement; targets confirmed across secondary sources.

formulas.name: LFM (Latent Fault Metric)

variables.meaning: failure rate of latent multiple-point faults
failure rate of safety-related hardware elements

formulas.worked_example: Given Σλ = 20 FIT, Σ(λ_SPF + λ_RF) = 0.2 FIT, Σλ_MPF,L = 1.98 FIT: denominator = 20 - 0.2 = 19.8; LFM = 1 - (1.98 / 19.8) = 1 - 0.1 = 0.90 = 90%.

formulas.name: PMHF (Probabilistic Metric for random Hardware Failures)
formulas.expression: PMHF ≈ Σ(λ_SPF + λ_RF + λ_MPF,detected residual contribution) over the item (exact summation depends on safety-mechanism coverage model); target is an absolute residual failure rate.

variables.meaning: average probability of a hazardous failure per hour over lifetime

formulas.worked_example: If residual uncontrolled failure rate sums to 8 FIT, PMHF = 8 FIT = 8 × 10^-9 h^-1, which satisfies ASIL D target < 10 FIT.
formulas.clause_locator: ISO 26262-5:2018 clause 9.4.2 / Table for PMHF targets
formulas.known_uncertainty: Precise algebraic expansion of PMHF when multiple safety mechanisms and duty cycles are present.

formulas.name: ASIL target values
formulas.expression: ASIL B: SPFM ≥ 90% (recommended), LFM ≥ 60% (recommended), PMHF < 100 FIT; ASIL C: SPFM ≥ 97%, LFM ≥ 80% (recommended), PMHF < 100 FIT; ASIL D: SPFM ≥ 99%, LFM ≥ 90%, PMHF < 10 FIT. ASIL A has no mandatory metric targets.
formulas.worked_example: A design with SPFM = 98%, LFM = 85%, PMHF = 50 FIT meets ASIL C but not ASIL D (SPFM and PMHF fail ASIL D thresholds).
formulas.clause_locator: ISO 26262-5 tables for hardware architectural metrics (SPFM/LFM) and PMHF
formulas.known_uncertainty: Whether ASIL B SPFM/LFM are strictly mandatory or recommended in the edition cited.

edge_cases: Σλ = 0 (no safety-related hardware) makes SPFM/LFM undefined — calculator must reject or flag.
Denominator of LFM (Σ(λ - λ_SPF - λ_RF)) = 0 when every fault is single-point or residual — LFM undefined or conventionally 100%.
Target comparison is ≥ for SPFM/LFM percentages and < for PMHF absolute rate; equality on SPFM/LFM passes, equality on PMHF target fails.

formulas.name: Chi-square upper-confidence FIT point estimate
formulas.expression: λ (failures per device-hour) = χ²(α, 2f+2) / (2 × ss × t × AF); FIT = λ × 10^9

variables.meaning: chi-square value at confidence level α with ν = 2f+2 degrees of freedom

formulas.clause_locator: JESD85 / JESD85A methods for calculating failure rates in units of FITs
formulas.known_uncertainty: Exact χ² quantile for 60% CL with 2 dof; worked AF must be recomputed from Arrhenius for the concrete temperatures.

formulas.name: Arrhenius acceleration factor

variables.meaning: activation energy of the failure mechanism

formulas.worked_example: Ea = 0.7 eV, T_test = 125 °C = 398.15 K, T_use = 55 °C = 328.15 K: (1/328.15 - 1/398.15) ≈ 0.000535; (Ea/k) ≈ 8120.3; AF = exp(8120.3 × 0.000535) ≈ exp(4.344) ≈ 77.0 (order-of; precise recalculation required for production use). Common industry reference often quotes ~40–80 depending on exact constants.
formulas.authority: JEDEC JESD85 / industry practice for HTOL derating
formulas.known_uncertainty: Exact numerical AF for 125 °C→55 °C at 0.7 eV depends on constant precision; typical published values around 77 or lower with slightly different k.

formulas.name: Typical activation energies and caveats
formulas.expression: Common default Ea = 0.7 eV for many silicon failure mechanisms when mechanism-specific data are unavailable; mechanism-specific Ea (e.g., 0.3–1.0 eV range) should be used when known.
formulas.worked_example: Using Ea = 0.7 eV for HTOL derating from 125 °C to 55 °C is the industry default cited in multiple vendor FIT notes when no better data exist.
formulas.known_uncertainty: Ea is mechanism- and technology-dependent; 0.7 eV is a conventional average, not universal.

edge_cases: f = 0 still yields a non-zero upper-bound FIT via χ²(α, 2); calculator must not return zero.
T_use ≥ T_test makes AF ≤ 1 (deceleration); calculator must allow but flag.
Confidence level α and degrees of freedom must match the chosen χ² table; mismatch produces incorrect upper bounds.

formulas.name: Total Processing Performance (TPP)
formulas.expression: TPP = 2 × MacTOPS × bit_length_of_the_operation, aggregated over all processing units on the IC (TPP = TPP1 + TPP2 + … + TPPn)

variables.meaning: theoretical peak tera (10^12) multiply-accumulate operations per second (D = A×B+C)
largest bit-length of the inputs to the multiply operation

formulas.worked_example: 300 MacTOPS at 16-bit: TPP = 2 × 300 × 16 = 9600. 150 MacTOPS at 16-bit: TPP = 2 × 150 × 16 = 4800 (exactly the a.1 threshold example given in the regulation).
formulas.clause_locator: 15 CFR Supplement No. 1 to Part 774, ECCN 3A090 Technical Notes to 3A090.a and 3A090.b
formulas.known_uncertainty: None on the formula text; bit-length definition is the largest input bit-length to the multiply.

formulas.name: Performance density
formulas.expression: performance density = TPP / die_area_relevant (as defined for the density threshold; exact denominator is the die area used in the regulatory definition)

variables.meaning: TPP per unit area for the 3A090 density threshold

formulas.worked_example: TPP = 1600 and performance density = 5.92 meets the a.2 threshold exactly.
formulas.clause_locator: 15 CFR Supplement No. 1 to Part 774, ECCN 3A090.a.2
formulas.known_uncertainty: Exact regulatory definition of the area denominator for density (die area vs. other); threshold values themselves are stated in the regulation.

formulas.name: 3A090.a control thresholds
formulas.expression: Controlled under 3A090.a if (TPP ≥ 4800) OR (TPP ≥ 1600 AND performance density ≥ 5.92)
formulas.worked_example: IC with TPP = 5000 → controlled by a.1. IC with TPP = 2000 and density = 6.0 → controlled by a.2. IC with TPP = 2000 and density = 5.0 → not controlled by these a-thresholds.
formulas.clause_locator: 15 CFR Supplement No. 1 to Part 774, ECCN 3A090.a
formulas.known_uncertainty: Additional .b/.c paragraphs exist with different thresholds; this entry covers the primary a-thresholds only.

edge_cases: Multiple bit-lengths on one IC: regulation requires evaluating the highest TPP value achievable.
Aggregation across all processing units on the die; omitting a unit understates TPP.
Threshold-exactly-equal semantics: TPP = 4800 or density = 5.92 meets the 'or more' / 'or more' test and is controlled.

formulas.name: Advanced manufacturing investment credit rate
formulas.expression: Credit = rate × qualified_investment_basis; rate = 25% for qualified property placed in service after 31 Dec 2022 and before the later increase, and 35% for property placed in service thereafter (per current statute after WFTC Act amendment).

variables.meaning: basis of qualified property placed in service that is part of an advanced manufacturing facility

formulas.worked_example: Qualified investment basis = $100 M placed in service in the 35% period: credit = 0.35 × 100 M = $35 M.
formulas.known_uncertainty: Exact transition date between 25% and 35% depends on the WFTC Act effective language; IRS pages state 25% through 2025 placements and 35% thereafter.

formulas.name: Advanced manufacturing facility definition (eligibility gate)
formulas.expression: Facility whose primary purpose is manufacturing of semiconductors or semiconductor manufacturing equipment (qualitative primary-purpose test; regulations may use >50% output tests).
formulas.worked_example: A fab whose primary output is semiconductor wafers qualifies; an office building or non-manufacturing structure on the same campus does not.
formulas.known_uncertainty: Quantitative safe-harbor percentages appear in regulations, not the statute text itself.

edge_cases: Property must be placed in service after 31 Dec 2022; earlier placements are outside the credit window.
Taxpayer must not be a 'foreign entity of concern' and must not have made an 'applicable transaction' in the year — binary eligibility gates outside pure arithmetic.
Credit is on basis of qualified property that is integral to the advanced manufacturing facility; non-integral or office portions are excluded from the basis.
